assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients discrete-choice demand estimation with endogenous prices and the dynamic-oversight and entry-exit framework are the workhorse of modern empirical industrial organization. They are used in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics, so the influence reaches well beyond one subfield.
assessment.attribution: The core demand-estimation contribution is most clearly Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995), building on Berry (1994). Pakes also led the dynamic-games and entry/exit framework (Ericson-Pakes, and Olley-Pakes on production). The longlist names seven people. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are credible contributors, but the three-person limit makes this a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use, replication, extension and practical application. Little risk that the contribution will be revised or overturned.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognize the demand-estimation strand alone or the broader structural IO programme, which would change who is credited.
Apart from the demand side, how much weight to give Bresnahan and Reiss's earlier empirical entry work.
My own field is close to this one, so I am cautious about overweighting familiarity; I am judging by the common criteria of influence and durability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped trade theory and empirics. They explain who trades, how gains from trade operate through reallocation, and why trade liberalization has distributional effects across firms. The framework is now standard in graduate teaching and policy modelling.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman's work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, together with his earlier monopolistic competition and trade work, makes up the broader programme. Redding's contributions are important but more recent, and Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not on this list although their empirical firm-level work is closely related.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation and extension. The trade field has already been recognized once, for Krugman in 2008, but this is a distinct contribution.
uncertainties: Possible overlap in credit with the Eaton-Kortum and Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line, which is not fully captured by this candidate's credited names.
Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the earlier new trade theory recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed the empirical measurement of opportunity, neighbourhood effects and mobility across areas and over time. The work has had very large influence on public policy debates and on the empirical practice of public and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is central across the programme, and Hendren and Friedman are key co-authors on mobility, neighbourhood effects and related work. Katz has longstanding related work on Moving to Opportunity and neighbourhood effects. A three-person limit makes it hard to credit everyone, and collaborative credit is hard to apportion.
assessment.maturity: The work is relatively recent, with most key results from 2014 onward. Some long-run findings and the causal interpretation of area effects are still being tested, so the track record is shorter than for many other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the main contribution should be judged as a measurement and data advance or as a body of causal findings.
Replication, durability and interpretation of area-level causal estimates over longer horizons.
Large collaborative teams complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and interest-rate rules is the core of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. It is highly consequential for practice and for the theory of price setting.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) provided the staggered pricing device. Taylor provided staggered contracts and the policy rule. Woodford codified the framework in a microfounded, welfare-based treatment. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are major contributors to estimation and extension, so the eight credited names make a three-person selection arbitrary at the margin.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use and refinement. The 2021-23 inflation episode and the heterogeneous-agent critique have tested parts of the framework without displacing it.
uncertainties: Difficulty of cleanly separating credit among many contributors.
Whether the committee views recent inflation experience or the heterogeneous-agent literature as qualifying the framework's standing.
Sticky-price evidence from micro data has been mixed on the size and nature of rigidities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence on local labour markets reshaped understanding of how trade and technology affect employment, wages and regional outcomes. The work has had high policy influence in debates over globalization and automation.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the central authors of the China shock papers. Autor also has foundational task-based work with Levy and Murnane, and with Acemoglu on tasks. Katz is a key early contributor on wage inequality and skill-biased change, and Acemoglu is not on this candidate's list.
assessment.maturity: A decade or more of replication and debate. Some magnitudes are contested and the long-run effects continue to be studied.
uncertainties: Debate over identification and magnitude in the shift-share design.
Credit split between task-based theory and trade-shock empirics, and with contributors outside the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Debiased machine learning and causal forests give valid inference for treatment effects with flexible, high-dimensional nuisance estimation, and they let researchers estimate treatment-effect heterogeneity. The methods are spreading quickly through applied economics, tech and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and co-authors developed double/debiased ML. Wager and Athey developed causal forests. Key co-authors such as Hansen, Newey, Imbens and Belloni are not credited here and may be critical to credit.
assessment.maturity: Core results date from roughly 2015 to 2018, so the track record is comparatively short, though adoption is fast.
uncertainties: Whether the work has been tested long enough, and whether its practical importance is as large as its methodological appeal suggests.
Attribution is likely to be contested because several unlisted co-authors contributed.
Possible overlap with credit for Imbens and Angrist, recognized in 2021.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, a key mechanism in macro-finance and in understanding credit cycles and financial crises. It is highly influential for both theory and policy modelling.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist developed the financial accelerator evidence and extensions, and Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist are the usual associated names, but Bernanke already shared the 2022 prize.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of use, and renewed relevance after the 2008 crisis. Mature.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2022 prize for banking and financial crisis research.
Whether the committee wants to credit the theory alone, or the empirical financial accelerator line as well.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth series, built from tax records and national accounts, reopened inequality as a central empirical topic and prompted new work on taxation and offshore wealth. The influence on research and public debate is very high.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the core of the top-incomes work, Zucman of the wealth and offshore wealth work. Atkinson, now deceased, was an important precursor and cannot be recognized. Credit for some measurement results is shared with a large World Inequality Database collaboration.
assessment.maturity: Broad confirmation of the headline facts, but there is continuing debate over the measurement of wealth and income concentration and over the theoretical interpretation, such as r>g.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over data construction and over the interpretation of long-run dynamics.
Whether the committee judges data construction as a prize-worthy discovery relative to the other candidates.
Public prominence may not reflect scientific consensus.
